checks.axioms: #assert_axioms PolicySubmission.policy in Submission/PolicyCheck.lean: fails the build on native_decide (Lean.ofReduceBool), sorry (sorryAx) or any declared axiom, so every band's side conditions really did go through the kernel
checks.correctness: Shor.policy_submission_correct: proved once, generic in the policy; no per-submission proof. Shor.submission_correct is the one-band case at threshold 0
checks.shrink_advisory: bands[].shrinks is Shor.Policy.bandShrinks: does this band's table shrink the operand width at every width the band covers? false means the recursion falls through to the schoolbook leaf somewhere in the band's own range, so the band is dead weight there. A performance warning, NOT an admissibility condition - the policy is correct either way
checks.side_conditions: per band: C1 length, C2 det ≠ 0 (proved from pairwise projective distinctness), C3 ordered point consumption + safe adds, C4 returns to start — all four proved for every band in Submission/PolicyTemplate.lean by the submitter and reduced by Lean's kernel at build time
checks.sorted: ShorPolicySubmission.sorted: the thresholds strictly decrease, closed by decide. This is the only obligation a policy adds on top of its bands' own C1-C4, and it is what makes band i cover [t_i, t_{i-1}) literally

ir_status: NOT EXTRACTED. The single-table surface extracts an IR and pins it against the real compiled circuit at sampled widths (Shor.Reflect.submissionChecks). A policy's IR is a different object - one template per band plus a width dispatcher, with n left symbolic - and producing it is a separate piece of work (the IR plan). Until that lands, a policy submission carries its correctness theorem but not a resource estimate: admissible and unscored.
leaf: widths below the last threshold use the schoolbook leaf; with these bands that is n < 98
provenance: read by reflection from the named constants in Submission/PolicyTemplate.lean; the policy printed here is the policy C1-C4 and sortedness were proved about.
score: UNSCORED. The score would be trial_count × (single-run gate count of the IR), and there is no IR for a policy yet — see ir_status below.
